perf.summary: O(k) weighted walk can be reduced to O(n) using cycle periodicity plus a precomputed full-cycle weight sum.
perf.currentCost: for (long i = 0; i < k; i++) { sum += w[curr]; curr = f[curr]; } chases k dependent links and accumulates k loads from w. Unbounded in k despite the trajectory repeating every L <= n steps with a fixed per-cycle weight sum.
perf.proposedChange: Walk the tail (mu steps) accumulating w, reaching the cycle entry. Compute cycleSum = sum of w over the L cycle nodes once. For the remaining r = k - mu steps: add (r / L) * cycleSum, then walk r % L more steps adding their w. Total O(mu + L) = O(n). Guard: if (k <= n) keep the simple loop to avoid setup overhead.
perf.rationale: The weight accumulated per full cycle traversal is constant, so full laps can be multiplied instead of walked. Drops O(k) to O(n) for k > n, the dominant case for large k.
perf.risk: Result identical for all valid k. Overflow caveat: (r / L) * cycleSum and the running sum are long; if the original O(k) sum could already overflow long, the reduced form overflows identically (two's-complement multiply/add are associative under wraparound), so observable behavior is preserved only if callers tolerate the same wraparound — which the straight loop already exhibits. r/L and r%L use non-negative operands (r>=0, L>0), so no signed-division edge case. Requires w and f valid over visited indices (already assumed).

perf.summary: Two interleaved dependent loads (w[curr] then f[curr]) form one long dependency chain per step; minor reordering does not break it but the chain is inherent to the simple loop.
perf.currentCost: Each iteration: load w[curr], add, then load f[curr] to advance. curr is carried, so f[curr] is on the critical path; w[curr] can issue in parallel but both index the same register. Throughput is bound by the f[curr]->curr->f[curr] chain (~load latency per step).
perf.proposedChange: If staying with the O(k) loop, the only real win is the complexity reduction above; there is no branchless or strength-reduction trick that shortens an inherently serial pointer chase. Do not add speculative unrolling — the dependency on curr prevents ILP. Flagged only to record that the per-step cost is latency-bound and cannot be improved without the algorithmic change.
perf.rationale: Documents that micro-opts here are cargo-cult; the genuine lever is asymptotic, not constant-factor.
perf.risk: None proposed; this is an explicit non-opportunity to prevent wasted effort.
